clue.text: Step on board trendy futuristic craft

indicators.note: being on board means sitting inside the vessel, so the step goes within the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the craft one is on board
a pace is a single step
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb aboard some fashionable vehicle of the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention: put the piece inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for travel beyond Earth is the stock vehicle of science fiction, hence futuristic.

clue.text: Now 6 across 22 across 2 keeps going off

indicators.note: something going off has exploded or gone bad, so the letters of keeps are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cryptic aside about a place now renamed that keeps on going off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as the airport at 6/11 and 22's name today: Liverpool's airport was renamed after the Beatle in 2001, so this is its old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's airport carried this suburb's name until its renaming after the city's famous Beatle.

clue.text: Dry wine found in various places here

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A drinker's note that dry wine turns up all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the puzzle itself: several entries in this grid are hubs for flights named after people.
explanation.definitionFit: Several of this grid's entries are flight hubs named after famous people, so such terminals are scattered through it.

clue.text: Up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone is up before the court, a defendant in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something standing upright, raised vertically rather than lying flat.

clue.text: Hancock's first pint is unhealthy

indicators.note: the first letter of Hancock's is taken

parts.note: in Tony Hancock's sketch The Blood Donor he protests that a pint of blood is very nearly an armful

explanation.surface: A comedian's opening pint does him no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Hancock was a British TV comedian; in 'The Blood Donor' he complains 'A pint? That's very nearly an armful!'
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaging to the body is bad for one's wellbeing: a synonym.

clue.text: Nice person beyond doubt, cares a lot at first …

parts.note: something proven is established beyond doubt

indicators.note: the opening letters of cares, a and lot are taken

explanation.surface: A pleasant, trustworthy person who cares a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective; Nice is in Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nice comes from the region of southern France around it, so is a native of that region.

clue.text: President Bush written off? Finally, with knowledge and study turned into delight

indicators.note: into says the gathered pieces go inside the word for delight

parts.note: joy is great delight

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: ken is an old word for knowledge or understanding

indicators.note: turned means the word for a study is flipped end to end

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Was George Bush a write-off? At last, with learning and study, he became a source of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' works on all three words before it. The gathered letters go 'into' delight after its first two letters, and 'turned' reverses the study.
explanation.definitionFit: The 35th US head of state, shot in Dallas in 1963; New York's main airport bears his name.

clue.text: … whose day's borne by rising desire to travel

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece carried on another sits above it

parts.note: whose refers back to the Nice person of the previous clue, a French speaker, whose word for day is jour

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word desire's synonym is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone's day carried along by a growing urge to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 5: 'whose' is the person from Nice, so their day is French JOUR. 'Rising' turns YEN to NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a trip from one place to another is to go on a voyage: verb synonyms.

clue.text: Had arrived somehow without a memory

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrived in some other way, an anagram
without says the letter of a is left out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone turned up but cannot remember how they got there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges HAD ARRIVED after 'without a' takes one A out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer's disk drive is its long-term storage, the machine's memory.

clue.text: The man, a Romeo, gets the woman to embrace a spoken agreement

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the woman's letters go round the second a

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A romantic man persuades the woman to accept a verbal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken cries of approval in Parliament, voicing assent to what the speaker has said.

clue.text: Work & Love revue production

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of materials, so the letters of revue are reworked

explanation.surface: A billing for a theatrical show called Work & Love.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's body of output, or a single piece of it, is borrowed French for their creations.

clue.text: Behave in exile

definitions.meaning: to conduct oneself, as in to bear oneself well
to expel someone from a country

explanation.surface: How to conduct oneself when banished abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to conduct oneself, a formal sense, and to expel from a country.

clue.text: See 6
Rebel to retreat from the start? No chance!

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters picked out are read right to left
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Should a rebel back down from the beginning? Not a hope!
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' takes ARTNOC out of 'start? No chance', and 'to retreat' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Contras were the US-backed guerrillas fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s, so one is an insurgent.

clue.text: Open present at the indicated position

parts.note: overt means done openly
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Instructions to unwrap a gift where someone is pointing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase points to a place some distance away, as one gestures towards a location.

clue.text: Current objective is to cover Sartre composition

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so the word for objective encloses the rest

parts.note: an aim is an objective

indicators.note: a composition puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the letters of Sartre are reordered

explanation.surface: A goal of writing about a work by the French philosopher Jean-Paul Sartre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is the noun, a flow, not 'present'. 'Composition' gives IRSTRE from the philosopher's name, which the objective wraps 'to cover'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow of moving air is a current, like one in water.

clue.text: Serendipitous, its centre draw

parts.note: something serendipitous happens by happy chance, so is fortunate
its refers to the word serendipitous, whose three middle letters are D, I and P

explanation.surface: A fortunate event, its focus being a raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' points back at the word Serendipitous: its central three letters give DIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A British fairground game of chance where one pulls an unseen prize from a tub, so a kind of prize draw.

clue.text: Place of departure that without Henry Ford would have been a sinister one

indicators.note: without the H for Henry, the answer would need another letter in its place

parts.note: the cell block for prisoners awaiting execution is a sinister place of departure
Ford is read as for D, saying D stands where the H would be
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A grim thought about an airport if a car maker had been missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Ford' as 'for D': swap the H (henry) for D and London's main airport becomes the cells for the condemned, a sinister place of departure.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main international airport is where flights take off, so travellers depart from it.

clue.text: Shady retreat for a squirrel?

indicators.note: shady means dodgy or crooked, so the letters of retreat are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A cool spot in the leaves where a squirrel might hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-in-cheek description of a squirrel: a rodent that lives up in the branches.

clue.text: As one whose partner's gone to marry, suppressing instinct that hurts

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the word for marry encloses the rest

parts.note: to wed is to marry
the id is the instinctive part of the mind in Freudian theory
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone bereaved goes to marry again, holding back a painful urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having lost a spouse to death, one is left a widow or widower, the state described.

clue.text: Some favoured rallying round the pantry

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the letters picked out are read backwards
some says only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: Some favourite people gather in the kitchen store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes REDRAL from 'favoured rallying', and 'round' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool room or cupboard for keeping food is a synonym of storeroom for provisions.

clue.text: Lock for phone permit included in covering letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them; that the pair also sits inside covering letter is no coincidence but the setter's second route
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A locksmith's note about phoning for a permit, enclosed with a covering letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' is hair, not a door fitting. 'Included in covering letter' is a second route: the answer is hidden inside those two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock of hair is a strand, and a curled strand is this kind of curl.

clue.text: Vouched for watching cricket with England disheartened

parts.note: someone watching an international cricket match is at a Test

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart is removed, leaving only the outside letters of England

explanation.surface: A cricket fan's alibi: they were at the match with England in poor spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch for something is to confirm or certify its truth: a synonym.

clue.text: At last, Liverpool home town given hero musician

definitions.text: At last, Liverpool home town given hero musician

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of each of the six words that follow

explanation.surface: Liverpool finally names its airport after its hometown hero, a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' takes the final letters of Liverpool, home, town, given, hero and musician. The whole clue also defines: Liverpool's airport was renamed after the Beatle in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatle born in Liverpool, after whom the city finally named its airport in 2001.

clue.text: The French girl, sanctioned …

parts.note: le is the French for the
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A French girl has been punished, and the ellipsis leads to her next move.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by law is lawful, authorised by the rules.

clue.text: … had got drunk, taking top off

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a drink that got drunk was downed, swallowed

explanation.surface: Continuing the French girl's story: she drank too much and took her top off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got drunk' is not intoxication: a drink that got drunk was DOWNED, and 'taking top off' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to possess it: past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Autopilot leading winger

parts.note: pilots' slang name for an aircraft's automatic pilot is a man's name
being top or foremost is being the finest, first in the field

explanation.surface: An aircraft's automatic pilot steering ahead of a wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' is not part of a plane: it is the Manchester United wing forward from Belfast, whose city airport is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northern Irish footballer played on the wing for Manchester United, a famous outside forward.

clue.text: Moving first to lose out would lead to rebuke

indicators.note: the clue says taking that letter out of the answer leaves the rebuke, so the rebuke has it put back inside

parts.note: a wigging is a British informal word for a telling-off

indicators.note: the first letter of lose is taken

explanation.surface: A wriggling player is first to go out and will get a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: take the first letter of 'lose' out of the answer and you get WIGGING, a British word for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisting and squirming from side to side is a kind of motion, so the participles match.

clue.text: See 24
Glorified first replaced by second, becoming varied

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter in the word for glorified gives way to another piece

parts.note: adulated means praised excessively
A is first, as in an A grade or the first letter
mo is a short moment, a second

explanation.surface: A glorified winner was replaced by the runner-up, so things changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is A, as in an A grade; 'second' is MO, a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Changed in pitch or tone, as a voice is adjusted or varied in delivery.
